tool.name: sincei scBulkCoverage
tool.description: pseudo-bulk coverage tracks per group of cells

param.label: Cell groups
param.help: Either the UMAP/cluster table from scClusterCells (cell, UMAP1, UMAP2, cluster) or a 3-column table (sample, barcode, group), with a header line that does not start with #. Samples must match the BAM dataset names without .bam.

param.label: Normalization method
param.help: How to normalize the pseudo-bulk signal of each group.
param.option: CPM (counts per million reads in the group)
Frequency (binarized coverage per bin divided by the number of cells)
Mean (mean signal per bin across cells)

param.label: Chromosomes to ignore for normalization
param.help: Comma-separated chromosome names to skip when computing normalization factors, e.g. chrX,chrM.

param.label: Scale factor
param.help: The normalized signal is multiplied by this value.

param.label: MNase-seq / CUT&RUN mode
param.help: Count only the 3 central nucleotides of each 130-200 bp fragment, giving nucleosome positions. Requires paired-end data. A bin size of 1 is recommended.

param.label: Signal offset
param.help: Use this position (1-based, negative counts from the read end) inside each read as the signal, e.g. 12 for Ribo-seq. Two space-separated values define a range, e.g. '5 -1'. 0 is not allowed.

validator.message: One or two non-zero integers separated by a space

tool.help:
**What it does**
`scBulkCoverage` aggregates the reads of cells that belong to the same group (e.g. a cluster from `scClusterCells`, or a batch) and writes one pseudo-bulk coverage track per group. Coverage is counted in bins and can be normalized per group. The tracks can be viewed in a genome browser or used with deepTools.
-----
**Inputs**
- One or more BAM files with a cell barcode tag. - A table assigning cells to groups, in one of two forms: - the UMAP/cluster table from `scClusterCells` (`sample::barcode`, UMAP1, UMAP2, cluster) - a 3-column table: sample, barcode, group
Both tables must start with a header line. The first line is always read as the header, so a table without one loses its first cell. Lines starting with `#` are ignored, so the header must not start with `#`. The sample names must match the BAM dataset names without the `.bam` extension.
**Outputs**
- A collection with one bigWig or bedGraph track per group. @HELP_FOOTER@
